def: A sequence of measurements of one quantity taken at regular times, such as daily sales.
The moment a forecast is made; only data dated before it may be used.
How far ahead a forecast looks, for example 14 days.
The slow underlying direction of a series, such as steady growth or decline.
A pattern in a series that repeats with a fixed calendar period, such as weekly or yearly.
The correlation of a series with its own earlier values, which makes today's value informative about tomorrow's.
A forecast that repeats the value from one season ago, such as next Tuesday equal to last Tuesday.
Exponential smoothing with a level, a trend and a seasonal profile, each updated by its own weight.
A forecast's mean absolute error divided by that of the in-sample seasonal naive forecast, so that 1 means as good as seasonal naive.
The value of the series, or of a rolling statistic, from a fixed number of steps before the forecast origin, used as a model input.
Training a model for the target horizon itself, so each row uses only information available that many steps before its target.
Evaluating a forecasting method by repeatedly fitting on data before an origin, forecasting the next horizon and moving the origin forward.
A loss for quantile forecasts that charges q times the shortfall when too low and 1 minus q times the excess when too high.
A range expected to contain the future value with a stated probability, such as 80%.
